question: Choosing a next view is a decision problem, not another coverage-polygon test: which view-selection policy resolves a hidden wall world within a shared budget, at what action cost, and how often does it emit a definite answer the evidence does not support?
movement_rules: stations lie on a line; moves are only allowed between adjacent stations; one step costs move_cost

uncertainty-reduction.rule: greedy: observe the current station when it reduces expected posterior entropy (belief = uniform over compatible worlds), gain per cost; skip zero-gain observations; otherwise move toward the adjacent station whose window holds the most unseen bays, ties left; stop when resolved or no action is feasible

nearest-unseen.rule: observe the current station if its window holds any unseen bay; otherwise move one step toward the nearest station whose window holds unseen bays, ties left; stop when resolved or no action is feasible

fixed-order.rule: follow the frozen station order literally: move to each target, observe it, continue; stop early when resolved or the next action does not fit the budget; repeat or uninformative observations are not skipped

seeded-random.rule: uniform choice among feasible actions each step (repeat observations allowed); stop when resolved or no action is feasible

definitions.resolved: the compatible set has size 1 at the end of the run
definitions.answer: the single compatible world when resolved; otherwise the lexicographically smallest compatible world (a forced guess)
definitions.unsupported: a definite answer emitted while more than one world remains compatible
definitions.guess_correct: the emitted answer equals the hidden true world (recorded for diagnosis only; policies never see it)
definitions.impossible_view: no action sequence within the frozen budget drives the compatible set to the true world as a singleton; established by an exhaustive search over action sequences, used for analysis only

notes: Budget 4 is deliberately tight: the three-window tour needs 5-6 units, so every policy must choose which windows to buy and some worlds are unresolvable in principle.

Full-geometry view selection (continuous viewpoints, real frustums, occlusion, noisy captures) is a separately labelled upper bound and is NOT simulated here; this package studies the finite decision core.
Policies never read the true world: observations are the only channel through which truth enters the run.
Synthetic acquisition only: results describe this finite decision problem, never field improvement or electrical safety.
